This guide breaks down what it actually costs to run manual collections, how AI compares feature-by-feature, and which approach recovers more aged AR faster for dental practices in 2026. AI vs Manual Dental AR Collections Manual AR workflows leave denials unworked for days especially after hours and on weekends when payers process claims 24/7 AI-driven collections run continuously, catch denials in real time, and trigger patient follow-up automatically Clean claim rates: 98% with AI vs 80–85% with manual billing a gap that compounds into thousands of aged claims per year AI automation cuts denial rates from 18% to 7% in documented DSO implementations, without adding billing headcount For practices with AR90+ above 5% or billing across multiple locations, AI collections consistently outperform manual workflows Key Takeaways Aged AR over 90 days has only a 15-25% recovery probability and accounts past 120 days drop to just 33 cents on the dollar ( Southwest Recovery Services ) Verimedix recommends targeting a 14-21 day insurance AR turnaround, a 98%+ collection ratio, and keeping less than 15% of AR over 60 days old A dental billing specialist costs $63,529/year before benefits, training, and turnover and still leaves gaps in after-hours follow-up and high-volume periods AI-driven billing workflows achieve 98% clean claim rates vs. 80-85% for manual processes ( MedVoice ) One large dental group reduced denial rates from 18% to 7% within six months of deploying AI-assisted billing saving more than 1,500 staff hours annually ( Droidal ) Write-off rates at 120+ days reach 40-60% of AR value, versus 15-25% at the 90-day mark so earlier intervention is the entire game ( Resolve ) 58% of dental practices have committed to AI and automation for RCM workflows in 2026 , according to the Zentist 2026 Dental RCM Trends & Insights Report Why Dental Practices Are Moving to AI Collections Dental practices are moving to AI collections because manual billing cannot cover after-hours denials, scale across locations, or keep pace with growing claim volumes three structural problems no amount of individual billing effort can fully solve. Manual dental AR collections worked well enough when practice volumes were low and payer relationships were simple. For most practices today, neither of those conditions holds. Three structural problems drive the majority of the transition: The volume-coverage mismatch. A billing specialist managing claim submission, denial follow-up, patient balance outreach, insurance verification, and billing inquiries simultaneously cannot cover everything. When volume peaks after a holiday, after a new provider joins, during open enrollment aged AR accumulates faster than it can be worked down. This is not a performance failure; it is a structural ceiling. The after-hours dead zone. Insurance payers process claims seven days a week. Denial notices arrive on Saturdays. Timely-filing windows do not pause for weekends. Manual workflows that run 8am–5pm Monday through Friday miss a material share of the denial detection window and every day of delay is a day closer to write-off territory. The compounding backlog. Once 90-day AR starts accumulating, it tends to compound. Each month's new denials join the existing backlog. A practice six months behind on aged AR recovery cannot catch up manually without adding headcount and headcount additions carry their own ramp-up time, training costs, and retention risk. These problems show up consistently across practices beyond a certain billing volume, which is why 58% of dental practices have committed to RCM automation in 2026 . For most, the decision is not whether to automate it is which workflow gaps to close first. Arini: The #1 AI Platform for Dental AR Recovery Among AI dental AR collections platforms, Arini is the leading choice for DSOs and multi-location dental groups in 2026. It is the only platform that combines 24/7 AI-powered patient communication, real-time denial management, and direct PMS integration in one system. It connects natively with OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, and Dentrix built for dental revenue cycle workflows. Practices using Arini report denial rates cut from 18% to 7%, clean claim rates reaching 98%, and 40% faster claim processing compared to manual billing workflows. The platform handles patient balance follow-up through automated SMS, email, and outbound calls. It reaches patients after hours and on weekends when manual billing stops. For practices evaluating AI vs manual dental AR collections, Arini delivers measurable AR recovery results without requiring additional billing headcount. What Is Aged AR in Dental Practices? Aged AR in dental practices is accounts receivable that has remained uncollected beyond a defined threshold typically 60, 90, or 120 days from the date of service or initial claim submission. Accounts in the 90+ day bucket are the primary measure of AR health because the probability of collection falls sharply once claims reach that age. Most dental practice management platforms and billing benchmarks track AR aging in four buckets: 0-30 days (current), 31-60 days (early warning), 61-90 days (action required), and 90+ days (critical). Best-run dental practices keep AR over 90 days below 5% of total AR . Practices where this bucket exceeds 22% of total AR experience write-off rates three to four times higher than their peers. Aged AR has two components in dental: insurance AR (unpaid insurance claims) and patient AR (patient-responsible balances after insurance). Each ages differently and requires a distinct recovery approach. Insurance AR ages primarily because of denied claims that were not resubmitted promptly, missing documentation, or payer-specific errors in the original submission. These claims have a strict timely-filing window most payers set this at 90-365 days from date of service after which re-submission is no longer possible regardless of the merit of the claim. Patient AR ages because collection at point of service was not completed, follow-up was inconsistent or delayed, or billing statements were sent by mail with no automated escalation to phone or SMS outreach. The same coverage gaps that cause practices to miss patient billing calls also leave patient AR aging without consistent follow-up. Both require different workflows and both are areas where the difference between AI and manual collections is significant. The True Cost of Letting AR Age Past 90 Days The recovery curve for aged dental AR is steep and unforgiving. Here is what the data shows: At 90 days past due , AR accounts are worth approximately 87 cents on the dollar meaning 13% is already at risk of write-off At 120 days past due , that same account drops to 33 cents on the dollar a 67% effective write-off The probability of collection falls below 20% at 120 days, according to industry benchmarks widely cited by dental billing professionals Write-off rates jump from 15-25% at the 90-day mark to 40-60% beyond 120 days a nearly 3x increase in uncollected revenue For context: a dental practice billing $1.5 million annually with a collection ratio of 84% the industry average is leaving roughly $240,000 on the table each year. A material portion of that is aged AR that crossed the 90-day mark without adequate follow-up. Aged AR grows in most dental practices not because the money is uncollectable in principle. It grows because the manual workflows required to recover it are time-consuming and compete with a billing team's daily demands. Pulling aging reports, identifying priority claims, calling payers, resubmitting corrections, sending patient balance notices each step requires specialized knowledge. Each step competes with new claim submission, eligibility verification, and front-desk support running simultaneously. The Manual Collections Process: What It Actually Takes Running manual dental AR collections means assigning a billing specialist or more often, a front desk coordinator doing double duty to work through an AR aging report on a schedule. In practice, this is what that workflow looks like: Pull an AR aging report from the practice management system Sort by age (90+ days first) and by dollar value (highest balances first) For insurance AR: identify denial reason from the EOB or payer portal , gather any missing documentation, correct coding errors, and resubmit all done claim by claim For patient AR: generate and mail a paper statement, then call the patient if no payment arrives within 10–14 days a cycle that can repeat two to three times before escalation to a collection agency Update the practice management system with each follow-up action so the audit trail is maintained Track timely-filing deadlines manually, because a claim resubmitted after the payer's window closes cannot be recovered regardless of its validity This process is not flawed in concept. But it has structural limitations that matter when AR aging is the problem: Coverage gaps. Insurance AR denial notices arrive seven days a week, including after hours. Manual workflows only cover business hours and if Friday's denials are not caught until Monday, a claim has already lost two days of its appeal window. Prioritization accuracy. Manual aging report review tends to focus on recent, large-dollar claims. Smaller claims from 90-120 days ago the ones approaching write-off territory often sit at the bottom of the list and never get worked. Scalability ceiling. A single dental billing specialist at $63,529/year can typically manage a set number of accounts before productivity drops. As a group adds locations, the headcount required scales linearly and so do the salary costs. Clean claim rate. The industry average for manual billing is 80-85% clean claims on first submission . That means 15-20% of claims require at least one round of correction and resubmission each round, adding days to the collection timeline and increasing the probability that the account ages into a higher-risk bucket. We have a billing specialist why add AI on top? A billing specialist managing a full-volume practice handles claim submission, denial follow-up, patient balance outreach, insurance verification, and billing inquiries simultaneously. That is structurally too much for one person to cover without gaps. The gaps are specific: after-hours denials go unworked. Patient follow-up falls behind at month-end. Timely-filing deadlines get missed during high-volume periods. AI does not replace the billing specialist. It covers the structural gaps a single FTE cannot fill during business hours. Most practices that implement AI keep their billing team and redirect staff time to the higher-judgment work that benefits from human attention. Should dental practices outsource AR or use AI automation? The decision depends on practice size and current AR performance. Traditional outsourced billing firms charge 2–3.5% of collections which works for smaller practices but becomes expensive at scale. AI automation has a lower marginal cost per claim at higher volumes. It integrates directly with your PMS, embedding the workflow in your existing system rather than running as a separate service. For practices prioritizing speed, accuracy, and after-hours coverage, AI automation outperforms traditional outsourcing on all three dimensions. What is the timely-filing window for dental claims? Most dental insurance payers set timely-filing windows of 90-365 days from the date of service after which claims cannot be submitted or resubmitted regardless of their merit. This makes response speed to denials critical: a claim denied at day 60 that is not resubmitted within 30 days may fall outside the timely-filing window permanently, converting a recoverable claim into a write-off. AI-driven denial management which flags and routes denials in real time directly reduces the number of claims lost to timely-filing deadline expiration. How much does AI dental billing automation cost? A dental billing specialist costs $63,529/year in median salary approximately $75,000–$100,000 fully loaded with benefits and payroll taxes, per location. AI dental AR automation runs on subscription pricing that does not scale linearly with location count. Most practices find that the revenue recovered from improved clean claim rates and reduced write-offs exceeds the platform cost within the first year. How long until AI dental AR automation shows results? Most dental practices see measurable improvement in AR metrics within 60–90 days of deploying AI billing automation. Documented DSO implementations show denial rates cut from 18% to 7% and active denial volume reduced by 47% within six months. Clean claim rate improvements from 80–85% to 98% typically appear within the first billing cycle as AI pre-submission checks flag and correct errors before claims are submitted. Which PMS platforms integrate with AI dental billing? Leading AI dental billing platforms integrate directly with the major dental PMS platforms: OpenDental, Dentrix, EagleSoft, Denticon, and Dentrix Ascend. Arini connects natively with all five, synchronizing patient records, insurance data, and payment information in real time. This direct integration eliminates the manual data entry errors and update delays that generate avoidable claim rejections in practices running billing separately from their PMS. How does Arini help with dental AR recovery? Arini's AI platform contributes to dental AR recovery through 24/7 patient communication (answering balance inquiries, confirming payments, sending follow-up outreach), direct PMS integration with OpenDental, EagleSoft, Dentrix Ascend , and Denticon for real-time data synchronization, and insurance verification completed at the point of call before appointments, so eligibility issues are caught before claims are submitted. This prevents a material portion of the first-pass denials that generate aged AR in the first place. For practices looking to reduce dental AR days, Arini addresses the front-end of the revenue cycle while your billing team manages the back-end claim follow-up. Ready to see how AI-driven AR workflows perform for your practice size and PMS configuration? See It in Action

title: Allegro MicroSystems Unveils Innovative Power Products for a More Energy Efficient Future
summary: Allegro announced a groundbreaking series of Power products poised to redefine performance and efficiency across automotive, industrial and data center applications.
body_text: Allegro’s New Solutions Deliver Design Simplicity With Cost Savings MANCHESTER, NH – November 4, 2024 – Allegro MicroSystems, Inc. (“Allegro”) (Nasdaq: ALGM), a global leader in power and sensing solutions, today announced a groundbreaking series of Power products poised to redefine performance and efficiency across automotive, industrial and data center applications. Allegro’s innovative products, debuting at Electronica 2024, empower customers to achieve unparalleled performance while simplifying design and reducing costs. The new product lineup not only addresses the escalating demands for higher voltage and power, but also delivers industry-leading efficiency and reliability, marking a significant advance in power electronics technology. Allegro’s comprehensive suite of products encompasses cutting-edge true 48V motor drivers like the A89212 , A89224 and A89333 designed to address the thermal management needs of hybrid electric vehicles and AI Servers. Complementing these drivers is the APM81815 , a 48V buck regulator designed for superior EMI performance in dual-voltage hybrid electric vehicles. Rounding out the list of new products is the AHV85311 , a high-power isolated gate driver designed to accelerate the development of Silicon Carbide (SiC)-based power electronics. From optimizing efficiency in automotive applications to simplifying industrial designs as well as enhancing reliability in data centers, Allegro's new power IC innovations enable engineers to design smarter, more efficient systems. “The new power IC solutions from Allegro represent a significant leap forward in power electronics design," says Ram Sathappan, Sr. Director of Global Marketing & Applications at Allegro MicroSystems. "We're not just meeting the evolving demands of higher voltage and power; we're redefining what's possible. Our customers demand solutions that simplify design, enhance efficiency and lower costs, all of which our new products deliver. We're excited to partner with our customers to shape the future of power electronics and look forward to showcasing our innovative solutions at Electronica.” Key Allegro solutions launching at Electronica include: A89212 : Longer Battery Life and Lower System Costs This 48V SoC delivers high efficiency and torque at low speeds for power tools, eBikes and other industrial systems. In addition to extending battery life, this sensorless solution improves motor control precision and reduces cost by eliminating external hall sensors. With up to 256K of flash memory and 90V support, it is the first of its kind. A89224 : Optimized Efficiency for 48V Automotive Systems This SoC empowers the next generation of 48V automotive systems, optimizing fan and pump performance. Advanced motor control libraries maximize efficiency and torque at zero speed for pumps while minimizing noise for fans. This translates to reduced power losses, lighter wire harnesses and increased vehicle mileage for OEMs and ODMs. With 256K of flash memory, it offers robust processing power for complex tasks. A89333 : Increased AI Server Reliability with Code-Free 48V Fan Driver This motor driver offers code-free integration, reduced power loss and improved thermal management for 48V fans in AI servers. The integrated buck converter is designed to maximize efficiency, extending component life and boosting server reliability. APM81815 : Easy 48V Power Supply Design with Fewer Components This synchronous buck regulator simplifies 48V power regulation, offering a cost-effective solution with minimal design effort and a tiny footprint. Integrated capacitors and 2.2MHz switching frequency achieve industry-leading power density and superior EMI performance, making it ideal for electric power steering, braking, EV powertrains, thermal management, EV charging and robotics. AHV85311 : Smaller Simpler Design with Higher Efficiency Supporting multiple SiC MOSFET vendors, this universal gate driver utilizing Power-Thru technology offers a compact, efficient solution that simplifies development and enhances overall system performance. By eliminating the need for an external transformer or isolated bias supply, it reduces size, noise and design complexity while boosting efficiency. Ideal for a range of applications, including onboard chargers (OBC), DC-DC converters, data center power supplies, solar inverters and industrial motors, it accelerates time to market with superior isolation characteristics and seamless integration for SiC power systems design. Allegro’s new power and motor control solutions represent a significant step forward in addressing many of the challenges faced in today's rapidly evolving automotive and industrial landscapes. Attendees at Electronica are invited to visit the Allegro MicroSystems booth # C5.479 to meet with members of the Allegro executive team, view live demos and discover how its 48V solutions continue to drive innovation that enables customers to optimize performance, efficiency and cost. About Allegro MicroSystems Allegro MicroSystems, Inc. is leveraging more than three decades of expertise in magnetic sensing and power ICs, to propel automotive, clean energy and industrial automation forward with solutions that enhance efficiency, performance and sustainability. Allegro’s commitment to quality drives transformation across industries, reinforcing our status as a pioneer in "automotive grade" technology and a partner in our customers' success. For additional information, please visit https://www.allegromicro.com/en/ . title: Vouch Bites Back: Moves to Dismiss Corgi Lawsuit and Alleges Corgi Co-Founder Probed Vouch's Platform to Get Head Start
summary: Vouch, Inc. has filed a motion to dismiss in its entirety the trade-secret lawsuit brought against it by Corgi Insurance.
body_text: Vouch, Inc. has filed a motion to dismiss in its entirety the trade-secret lawsuit brought against it by Corgi Insurance. In court filings submitted on July 10, Vouch argues that Corgi’s case rests on documents that Corgi provides to every customer, that the case belongs in arbitration under Corgi's own terms, and that it was Corgi's co-founder, not Vouch, who allegedly used a competitor's quoting system to obtain a head start. The filings respond to a suit Corgi Insurance Services, Inc. and Technology Risk Retention Group, Inc. filed in April and amended in June in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. Corgi alleges that Vouch's Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, Kelly Wulff, posed as an applicant on Corgi's platform, obtained a policy, and extracted proprietary information before canceling the policy days later. Corgi's claims include trade secret misappropriation under the federal Defend Trade Secrets Act and Delaware law, plus fraud, civil conspiracy, unjust enrichment, and, in its amended complaint, false advertising and tortious interference. Vouch’s court filings contend that Corgi’s account is false. "Corgi rushed to court on bad information," the company said in its motion to dismiss. "The story conjured in Corgi's First Amended Complaint does not stand up to scrutiny, or square with common sense." "Not trade secrets at all" At the center of the dispute, according to Vouch’s court filings, is what Wulff actually obtained. Corgi describes a scheme to capture confidential underwriting intelligence. Vouch’s motion to dismiss describes something more ordinary: filling out an insurance application that Corgi invites all website visitors to complete, and receiving policy documents that Corgi "routinely sends to every purchaser of Corgi insurance, without any confidentiality markings, and without any limitation on how the documents may be shared." "These are not trade secrets at all," the motion said. Vouch’s motion also disputes the premise that Vouch had anything to gain. Corgi's "suggestion that Vouch was trying to 'steal' its online insurance questionnaire is absurd," the motion states, noting that Vouch has run its own online intake flow "for over 7 years." A trade secret claim, Vouch’s motion argues, requires both genuinely secret information and reasonable measures to protect it. The motion contends Corgi's amended complaint pleads neither and suffers from numerous additional defects. Vouch’s motion makes a similar argument about Corgi's false advertising claim, which, according to the motion, centers on one statement made by a Vouch salesperson calling the difference between the two companies' products "the difference between insurance that checks a box and insurance that actually pays." That statement, Vouch’s motion argues, is non-actionable "puffery" of the kind courts routinely dismiss. Corgi’s Alleged Misuse of Vouch’s Platform Vouch's motion to dismiss also levels a striking counter-accusation. Shortly after Corgi incorporated in 2024, according to Vouch’s motion to dismiss, Corgi co-founder and Chief Operating Officer Emily Yuan "twice navigated through Vouch's online insurance application flow (using two different email addresses)," toggled coverages, and "obtained a half-dozen unique price quotes." At least one other senior Corgi employee did the same from a Corgi email address, the motion says, citing industry commentary calling Corgi's application flow and offerings "nearly identical" to Vouch's. "It was Corgi (not Vouch) that unlawfully used competitive information to get a head start," Vouch’s motion said. According to the filing, "Corgi's co-founder Ms. Yuan engaged in precisely the conduct that Corgi falsely accuses Defendants of carrying out." Vouch’s motion to dismiss says the point will be "the subject of discovery and proof at the appropriate time and place." Vouch Moves to Compel Arbitration In a separate brief filed concurrently with its motion to dismiss, Vouch argues that Corgi’s case never belonged in court because the same Corgi website terms of use that Corgi invokes against Vouch contain a broad and mandatory arbitration clause. Vouch’s motion to compel arbitration asks the court to send the dispute to arbitration and to make Corgi pay Vouch’s fees incurred in filing the motion. Vouch’s motion casts Corgi’s suit as one of three Corgi has brought against competitors in the past year , "brought for anticompetitive purposes, not to protect intellectual property." "We look forward to presenting the facts," a Vouch spokesperson said, "which will show that it is Corgi, not Vouch, that has engaged in wrongdoing." The case is Technology Risk Retention Group, Inc. and Corgi Insurance Services, Inc. v. Vouch, Inc., et al., C.A. No. 1:26-cv-00426-RGA, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. Vouch is represented by Keker, Van Nest & Peters LLP and Young Conaway Stargatt & Taylor, LLP. Read Vouch's motion to dismiss here and its motion to compel arbitration here and here .

title: Advancing neurosurgery: Stryker supports brain tumor research through ongoing partnership
summary: Learn how Stryker's Neurosurgical team is partnering again with the National Brain Tumor Society to help raise awareness and funds for brain tumor research.
body_text: false /content/experience-fragments/stryker/corporate/en/about/news/_2024/features/stryker_is_doubling_/experience-fragment/mobile Advancing neurosurgery: Stryker supports brain tumor research through ongoing partnership The facts are staggering. An estimated 1.3 million Americans are living with a brain tumor and approximately 109,000 more will be diagnosed in 2026.1 What’s more, pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of cancer-related death among children and adolescents ages 0-19 years.1 Yet even with those statistics, brain tumor research remains underfunded. This is why Stryker’s Neurosurgical team is proud to partner again with the National Brain Tumor Society (NBTS) and help raise awareness and funds for brain tumor research. "We're proud to partner with the society to support, empower, and amplify the voice of the brain tumor community as we work to advance neurosurgery and transform lives," said Mitch Foley, Vice President and General Manager of Stryker's Neurosurgical business. As part of this ongoing partnership, Stryker will donate $25,000 to the NBTS to help drive awareness and funding for brain cancer research. The NBTS has already awarded more than $38 million in research grants to researchers at leading institutions, all in the pursuit of more effective treatments and ultimately a cure. Stryker’s commitment to advancing neurosurgical care is also reflected in its innovative products. In 2019, Stryker released the Sonopet iQ Ultrasonic Aspirator , a technology that helps surgeons remove soft and hard tissue as well as work near critical anatomy. This advancement is helping to advance neurosurgical care. To learn more about the National Brain Tumor Society or to make a donation, please visit their home page or giving platform . Together, we can support groundbreaking research and bring hope to countless individuals affected by brain tumors. “Brain cancer patients and their families exhibit strength and courage throughout their journey. It’s a privilege to support initiatives like this that are working to find a cure,” said Jeff Gorton, President of Stryker’s Instruments division. David F. Arons, JD, Chief Executive Officer of the National Brain Tumor Society says, “Brain tumors are some of the toughest and most complex diseases on the planet. The generous support of sponsors like Stryker will help advance our mission and the pursuit of better outcomes for patients.” What does it mean to #GoGrayInMay? According to the National Brain Tumor Society, “the brain tumor experience is full of extraordinary darkness and extraordinary hope. The gray area that falls in between is what drives us, unrelentingly, toward our shared mission of conquering and curing brain tumors—once and for all.”² Use #GoGrayInMay or #GrayMay to show how you’re taking action and raising awareness to make lasting change for the brain tumor community.

body_text: Managing a global team means facing one unavoidable challenge: paying overseas contractors efficiently and compliantly. When freelancers and independent workers are scattered across different countries, each with unique tax laws, currency requirements, and payment preferences, the complexity multiplies fast. Companies need practical solutions that can simplify international payroll, maintain compliance across borders, and ensure remote workforces get paid on time without friction. Rather than juggling multiple payment platforms, compliance tools, and currency conversion services, businesses benefit from unified solutions designed to manage international contractors and employees. body_text: Airbus Photo Davenport Aviation announced the Phoenix Police Department has placed an order for a new Airbus H145 helicopter, further strengthening one of the nation’s premier airborne law enforcement programs. The addition of the H145 reflects the department’s continued investment in modern aviation capabilities that enhance public safety, operational readiness, and mission effectiveness. Designed to support a wide range of airborne law enforcement operations, the H145 will provide exceptional performance, advanced technology, and increased mission flexibility for years to come. The Phoenix metropolitan area presents one of the nation’s most demanding operating environments, where extreme heat, mountainous terrain, and expansive urban and desert landscapes require aircraft capable of exceptional performance and reliability. The new H145 will join the Phoenix Police Department’s existing fleet of Airbus H125 helicopters, adding a twin-engine capability to complement the department’s already extensive airborne operations. Together, the fleet will enhance the department’s ability to support complex search-and-rescue missions, tactical operations, and public safety response across the Valley. “We’re honored to continue supporting the Phoenix Police Department as they invest in the future of their aviation program,” said Chris Arnold, director of government sales at Davenport Aviation. “The H145 is an exceptional platform for the demanding missions Phoenix performs every day, and we’re proud to help deliver an aircraft that will serve the department and its community for years to come.” Home to one of the largest law enforcement helicopter fleets in the United States, the Phoenix Police Department continues to invest in modern aviation capabilities that strengthen mission readiness and operational safety. The addition of the H145 builds on an already proven Airbus fleet, providing enhanced redundancy, increased mission flexibility, and expanded capability for the department’s most demanding public safety operations. Davenport Aviation will support the Phoenix Police Department throughout the acquisition process, with aircraft delivery anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2028. Aircraft completion and mission equipment integration will be performed by Hangar One Avionics in Carlsbad, California, ensuring the aircraft is mission-ready and fully configured to meet the department’s operational requirements upon delivery. This press release was prepared and distributed by Davenport Aviation.

title: Capital One: SME Market Intelligence Through Transparent AI and Web Data.

body_text: For decades, the Small and Medium-sized Enterprise (SME) sector has represented a significant growth opportunity for the financial services and insurance industries. However, despite making up the vast majority of the business population, SMEs have remained one of the most difficult segments to track and understand. Traditionally, the lack of structured data has forced organisations to rely on fragmented ‘signals' or outdated company databases, leading to inefficient outreach and higher risk profiles. Recent breakthroughs in AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and machine reading are fundamentally changing this landscape. At Glass.AI, our AI technology is designed to bridge this information gap by mapping the digital footprint and activities of millions of SMEs in real-time. The Challenge of “Invisible” Data About Businesses Unlike large public corporations that file quarterly reports and maintain high-profile media presences, the activities of SMEs are often “hidden” within the open web. Their most critical growth and risk signals are scattered across disparate sources: Company websites and news mentions. Job boards and hiring announcements. Social media activity and e-commerce platforms. Product launches and geographical expansion signals. Historically, this data was too unstructured and voluminous for manual discovery at scale or tracking. For example, sales and marketing teams were often left “chasing ghosts”, relying on high-level company databases or sales intelligence tools rather than evidence-based insights on SMEs. Beyond LLMs and Company Databases: A Structural Approach to SME Research While many organisations are exploring generative AI, at Glass.AI, we apply a structural, transparent approach to business research. By combining deep web crawling with business ontologies, our AI moves beyond simple keyword matching to understand context and intent. This allows for the continuous monitoring of the SME ecosystem to: Detect Real-World Events: Identify office openings, new product launches, international expansion, key customer wins or leadership changes as they happen. Normalise Unstructured Data: Transform messy web content into structured, usable intelligence for CRM and risk models. Ensure Verifiable Insights: Unlike “black box” AI models, our approach provides a clear path back to the source data, ensuring compliance and data provenance. From Guesswork to Precision The application of AI-driven signal monitoring has shown material results in the financial sector. As an example, Capital One in the United States was able to engage with SMEs at the precise moment of a “trigger event” (such as a new product launch or office opening), and this led to a 160% increase in booking rates for proactive sales channels. By shifting from static databases to a living company data ecosystem, financial services organisations can achieve: Enhanced Risk Modelling: Identifying healthier businesses earlier to lower delinquency rates. Operational Efficiency: Reducing costs of acquisition by focusing resources on high-intent prospects. Personalisation at Scale: Engaging business owners with messages that reflect their current operational reality. The Shift Toward Evidence-Led Decision Making The SME market has not changed, but our capacity to observe and track it has. The transition from “guessing” to “knowing” allows financial institutions like Capital One and others to see SMEs as the dynamic, evolving entities they truly are. As we continue to map and track the SME ecosystems across countries, the organisations that succeed will be those that leverage AI to gain a clearer understanding of the sectors they serve. At Glass.AI, we remain committed to providing the data infrastructure that anchors these strategic decisions.

title: How evergreen funds can improve private market deployment in PPLI
summary: By: StepStone Insurance Solutions Key takeaways Executive summary Most private placement life insurance (PPLI) policies funded with private equity insurance dedicated funds (IDFs) face a practical challenge: capital may not be fully invested in private markets for several years. That delay can reduce the compounding benefit PPLI is designed to support. For advisors and high-net-worth […] The post How evergreen funds can improve private market deployment in PPLI appeared first on StepStone Group .
body_text: By: StepStone Insurance Solutions Key takeaways Traditional drawdown insurance dedicated funds (IDFs) create a deployment lag (the J-curve) inside private placement life insurance (PPLI), costing clients months or years of tax-advantaged compounding. Evergreen, open-ended IDFs invest premium dollars on day one through secondaries and co-investments, cutting cash drag and improving return on committed capital versus Internal Rate of Return (IRR)-focused drawdown funds. Evergreen structures fit PPLI’s long-duration needs: no fixed end date, weekly net asset value (NAV), no capital calls or Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Schedule K-1 tax forms (K-1s), and periodic liquidity windows. StepStone’s Balanced Private Markets Fund (SBAL) is a purpose-built, diversified four-asset-class evergreen IDF managed by StepStone Group in partnership with SALI Fund Services. Trade-offs remain: redemption gates can close, NAV is an estimate rather than a transaction price, IRS compliance is ongoing, and manager selection drives the dispersion of outcomes. Executive summary Most private placement life insurance (PPLI) policies funded with private equity insurance dedicated funds (IDFs) face a practical challenge: capital may not be fully invested in private markets for several years. That delay can reduce the compounding benefit PPLI is designed to support. For advisors and high-net-worth clients who already understand PPLI and IDFs, the strategic case for private markets inside a life insurance wrapper is well established. Tax-deferred compounding, income tax-free death benefits, asset protection, and access to institutional-quality investments can make PPLI a useful vehicle for long-term, multigenerational wealth planning. Less discussed is how the structure of the IDF can affect that compounding. Most PPLI policies with private market exposure rely on traditional drawdown funds. This paper introduces a novel approach: evergreen IDFs, which we believe fit the PPLI structure far more effectively. StepStone’s Balanced Private Markets Fund (SBAL) is among the first purpose-built options designed specifically for this pairing. The hidden cost of traditional IDF deployment In drawdown funds, managers typically call capital over two to five years. Until then, premium dollars may sit in money market funds or short-duration bonds, earning less than the private market return the client seeks. That early return drag is the well-known “J-curve.” Inside a PPLI policy, it carries an added cost: each month of cash drag is a month of potential tax-advantaged private market compounding the client does not capture. title: Engineering for a More Sustainable Future: From Dishwasher Fixes to the Hydrogen Frontier
summary: When Kassy Hart was a teenager, she thought the life of an engineer was a bit like a newspaper cartoon she used to read. “You’re just sitting at a desk not talking to anyone, and this boss will yell at you for no reason,” says Hart, who is now a data center and hydrogen commercialization manager at GE Vernova. “That was before I got to design something.”
body_text: When Kassy Hart was a teenager, she thought the life of an engineer was a bit like a newspaper cartoon she used to read. “You’re just sitting at a desk not talking to anyone, and this boss will yell at you for no reason,” says Hart, who is now a data center and hydrogen commercialization manager at GE Vernova. “That was before I got to design something.” It was the summer of 2006, and Hart, who was partway through a bachelor’s degree in languages and international economics, was interning in GE Appliances’ finance department. Boasting a high school diploma and credits in math and science — and loads of enthusiasm — Hart applied for an engineering intern position at the company. (“I ended up working two at the same time,” she remembers.) Hart’s new engineering boss didn’t yell at her but rather threw her a project: to redesign a foam widget that would stop dishwasher doors from bending when pushed. Still unaware of CAD tools, Hart hand-drew and cut a design, which worked like a charm. “It was simple and small, and it could be manufactured in batches,” she says. “We estimated it would save around $45,000 a year.” Encouraged by her success, Hart trained her sights higher and studied for a bachelor’s and later a master’s in mechanical engineering with a certificate in power and energy at the University of Kentucky. Policy became her biggest interest. “I wanted to influence decisions on how we’re going to control or enable technologies for the future, specifically in energy.” Now she’s doing exactly that. Today Hart is known for her engineering work on heavy-duty turbines that can burn hydrogen-rich blends, and as a font of knowledge about the fuel. She’s been recognized as one of this year’s Women in Hydrogen 50 , a list of 50 women industry leaders who have been nominated by their peers. Along with GE Vernova’s Lisa Berry , she was honored this week at the Women’s Global Leadership Conference in Energy (WGLC) in Houston. Hart at the April 2024 launch of GE Vernova as an independent company, at the New York Stock Exchange. Image credit: GE Vernova Hydrogen’s Unharnessed Potential It’s become increasingly clear that heavy-duty turbine operators can swap out natural gas for hydrogen and not sacrifice a single megawatt-hour of generation. But Hart is keen to ensure that hydrogen’s sustainability benefits are fully acknowledged. “Using just a small amount of hydrogen [in a heavy-duty turbine] can reduce emissions by more than you think,” she says. For example, the impact on a heavy-duty turbine’s carbon emissions when you mix a mere 5% hydrogen by volume with natural gas fuel is equivalent to taking thousands of cars off the road. (One of GE Vernova’s H-Class turbines burning a 50% mix of hydrogen and running in combined cycle would result in 43% fewer carbon emissions than natural gas — not to mention up to 69% fewer than coal.) Hart urges policymakers and power generators to grasp the benefits on the table. “If you can produce hydrogen on-site, why wouldn’t you?” she says, referring to the renewable and nuclear plants that generate the power to produce yellow, pink, and green hydrogen . She is also keen to banish the notion that hydrogen combustion is an “impossible” technology. “People compare it to what’s in play right now,” she says. “We have around three million miles of natural gas distribution and pipelines in the United States, versus only 1,600 miles of hydrogen pipelines,” she explains. Hart trusts in the laws of economic gravity, which dictate that long-term investment in the industry will drive costs down. Costs and sustainability are also closely intertwined, argues the engineer, citing the example of modern transportation. “Cars have such good gas mileage and improved technology because of our push to lower fuel costs, consumption, and emissions,” she says. “The same principle will determine hydrogen adoption.” Hart (second row, third from right) at the 2025 Summit for GE Vernova‘s Women’s Network, which comprises more than 10,000 women worldwide. Image credit: GE Vernova Hart, who is a proud global committee member of GE Vernova’s 10,000-strong Women’s Network, has been spreading these messages far and wide in recent years. She’s supported the industry’s response to hydrogen production incentives and even launched an internal information hub that provides updates on global hydrogen policy. As the laying of the groundwork continues, the onetime intern with a clever appliance solution is now turning her attention to building the industry. “The technology is here, and it’s being adopted — perhaps at a slower pace than we’d hoped, but it’s happening,” she says. Adds Hart: “We’ll see more success stories, more projects going into operation, which will help normalize lower-carbon fuels in power generation. That’ll be a win for sustainability around the globe.”

title: Farnborough Airshow 2026: All the News That Made Headlines
summary: GE Aerospace is showcasing its commitment to building a more durable and efficient future of flight at the 2026 Farnborough International Airshow, highlighting next-generation t
body_text: GE Aerospace is showcasing its commitment to building a more durable and efficient future of flight at the 2026 Farnborough International Airshow, highlighting next-generation technologies and breakthrough capabilities across commercial and defense aviation. Stay here for all the latest updates on announcements from GE Aerospace and CFM International, a 50-50 joint company between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines. Together with our customers, we’re reaching new heights in advancing the future of flight. July 24, 2026 GE Aerospace Wraps Historic Farnborough Airshow GE Aerospace (NYSE: GE) wrapped up the 2026 Farnborough International Airshow with record engine demand, continued momentum across durability and services, and major advances in hybrid electric flight. Jet2 Plc Confirms LEAP Engine for all its Airbus A321neo Aircraft UK leisure travel group Jet2 plc has today announced that it has selected the CFM LEAP-1A engine to power 54 Airbus A321neo aircraft. With this announcement, Jet2’s LEAP-1A-powered A321neo fleet will now span 146 aircraft, alongside nine leased aircraft. The agreement, which also includes a long-term maintenance service, supports Jet2’s growth strategy. July 22, 2026 GE Aerospace and Magellan Aerospace Sign Memorandum of Understanding for F414 Sustainment GE Aerospace (NYSE:GE) and Magellan Aerospace Corporation signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities in Canada for the F414-GE-39E engine that powers the Saab JAS 39 Gripen E fighter. The MOU is predicated on whether the Government of Canada proceeds with the acquisition of the Saab JAS 39 Gripen E fighter as part of the future Royal Canadian Air Force fighter fleet. Austrian Airlines Selects GE Aerospace FlightPulse® to Expand Flight Data Analytics to the Cockpit GE Aerospace today announced that Austrian Airlines, part of the Lufthansa Group, has signed for FlightPulse®, a GE Aerospace, Software as a Service (SaaS) mobile application that connects operational flight data directly to pilot decision-making before and after each flight. The announcement follows a signing at the Farnborough International Airshow. ITA Airways Adopts GE Aerospace Fuel Insight and FlightPulse® to Strengthen Data-Driven Decisions GE Aerospace announced today that ITA Airways has signed an agreement to implement Fuel Insight and FlightPulse, two GE Aerospace, Software as a Service (SaaS) solutions designed to help airlines turn data into actionable insight. The announcement was marked by a signing at the Farnborough International Airshow. FlyOne Armenia signs MoU with CFM International for LEAP-1A engines to power Airbus A321neo aircraft FlyOne Armenia, the largest airline in Armenia, signed an MoU (Memorandum of Understanding) with CFM International for four LEAP-1A engines to power two Airbus A321neo. The aircraft order was announced in May during the state visit of French President Emmanuel Macron in Yerevan. July 21, 2026 National Airlines Orders More GE Aerospace CF6 and GE90 Engines GE Aerospace announced today that National Airlines has committed to purchase one GE90-110B and six CF6-80C2 engines to power their Boeing 777F/747F cargo airplanes. ABL Aviation Selects GE Aerospace ATS in Five-Year Agreement to Support Higher-Volume Aircraft Transitions GE Aerospace, Software as a Service (SaaS), today announced that ABL Aviation has signed a five-year agreement to adopt GE Aerospace’s Asset Transfer System (ATS) to support aircraft transitions across its growing portfolio. Abra Group and CFM Expand Partnership With LEAP-1A Engine Order CFM International and Abra Group, parent of Avianca and GOL, today announced that Avianca has selected CFM LEAP-1A engines to power 50 previously unallocated aircraft in its remaining 134-aircraft Airbus A320neo family order – together with a comprehensive services package to support Abra Group’s long-term operational needs, that includes spare engines and long-term services, the latter of which will also cover GOL’s fleet of Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. BBAM Expands Engine Portfolio with Agreement to Acquire 30 CFM LEAP Spare Engines BBAM Limited Partnership (“BBAM”) today announced an agreement to purchase 30 CFM International LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B spare engines, strengthening its engine portfolio in support of operators of Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. GE Aerospace Announces AerCap Selects GEnx Engines to Power 15 Additional Boeing 787 Dreamliners GE Aerospace today announced that AerCap Holdings N.V. ("AerCap") has selected the GEnx-1B engine to power an additional 15 Boeing 787 Dreamliners. CALC Chooses CFM LEAP-1A Engines to Power Additional Airbus A320neo-Family Aircraft China Aircraft Leasing Group Holdings Limited (CALC) today announced the selection of CFM International LEAP-1A engines to power and additional 20 A320neo and A321neo aircraft. AIP Capital Agrees to Purchase 11 CFM LEAP-1B Spare Engines AIP Capital and Bridgepoint Group today announced an agreement to purchase 11 CFM International LEAP-1B spare engines to support operators of Boeing 737 MAX family aircraft. The engines will support AIP and Bridgepoint’s strategy of providing airlines, MROs, and other operators with in-demand spare engines to support their operating needs. GE Aerospace and Turkish Technic Sign Agreement to Expand Electronics MRO Capability in Türkiye GE Aerospace and Turkish Technic today announced a Service and License Agreement that will expand GE Aerospace-authorized maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) support for Data Link Control and Display Units (DCDU) for an initial five-year term. The agreement enables Turkish Technic, one of the world’s leading aviation services providers, to offer OEM-authorized services to domestic and global airline customers from its world-class facilities in Istanbul. July 20, 2026 IndiGo and CFM Sign MoU Paving the Way to a Record Agreement for 1,000+ LEAP-1A Engines IndiGo, India’s largest airline and one of the world’s fastest-growing carriers, today announced it has signed an MoU (Memorandum of Understanding) with CFM International for an order of 1,000+ LEAP-1A engines to power 510 Airbus A320neo Family aircraft. This will be the largest single order ever placed for LEAP engines and a record for CFM International. GE Aerospace and SPDB Financial Leasing Signs Agreement for CF34-10A Spare Engines GE Aerospace has signed an agreement with SPDB Financial Leasing for 10 CF34-10A spare engines, underscoring continued cooperation between the two companies and their shared focus on supporting fleet operations and future growth. Philippine Airlines Selects GE Aerospace GEnx engines to Power New 787-10 Dreamliners GE Aerospace announced today that Philippine Airlines (PAL) has selected the GEnx-1B engines to power its 15 new Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners, including purchase rights for five additional aircraft. Jackson Square Aviation Selects CFM LEAP-1A Engines to Power Airbus A320neo Family Aircraft Jackson Square Aviation (JSA) today announced the selection of CFM International’s LEAP-1A engines to power a number of Airbus A320neo Family aircraft from its previously announced Airbus order. GE Aerospace Fuel Insight to Help Air France KLM Group Reduce Fuel Costs and Drive decarbonization Ambitions GE Aerospace, Software as a Service (SaaS), today announced that the Air France KLM Group — Air France, Hop! and Transavia France — has signed a five-year agreement for Fuel Insight, GE Aerospace’s fuel analytics solution that helps airlines optimize fuel planning and performance and supports sustainability reporting. GE Aerospace Partners with NASA, BETA Technologies, and Boeing on World’s First High-Altitude Hybrid Electric Flight GE Aerospace announced today at the Farnborough International Airshow an industry first to advance the future of flight, demonstrating the viability of more electric aircraft engine systems for aviation. In collaboration with NASA, BETA Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BETA) (“BETA”) and Boeing, GE Aerospace conducted the first hybrid electric flight above 30,000 feet, reaching the same altitude levels of passenger commercial aircraft. During tests, the team’s single longest flight in hybrid electric operation was more than two hours. SMBC Aviation Capital Selects CFM LEAP-1A Engines to Power 35 Airbus A320neo Aircraft SMBC Aviation Capital, the leading global aviation finance platform, today announced it has finalized an agreement for CFM International LEAP-1A engines to power 35 Airbus A320neo family aircraft. Shield AI and GE Aerospace Light Off X-BAT Engine GE Aerospace and Shield AI have successfully completed integration, actuation, and engine light-off testing of the advanced Axisymmetric Vectoring Exhaust Nozzle (AVEN) for Shield AI’s X-BAT aircraft, a critical milestone in the program's path to vertical flight. BOC Aviation Announces Order for up to 300 LEAP Engines CFM International and BOC Aviation Limited have finalized a firm order for up to 200 LEAP-1A and 100 LEAP-1B engines to power Airbus A320neo family and Boeing 737 MAX aircraft that BOC Aviation had previously ordered. July 19, 2026 GEnx-1B Engines Surpass 50 Million Flight Hours The GE Aerospace GEnx-1B engine has surpassed the 50 million flight hour mark in just over 14 years, the fastest rate ever for GE Aerospace commercial widebody engine model. July 18, 2026 CFM Secures Certification for LEAP-1B Durability Upgrades CFM International has secured certification of the CFM LEAP-1B high-pressure turbine (HPT) durability kit from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA). The system will double time on wing in hot and harsh environments like in Middle East and India. CFM is beginning to industrialize production of the hardware, with full production cutover expected in early 2027. CFM expands, strengthens open MRO ecosystem CFM International continues to invest in its open maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) ecosystem, building both capability and capacity to meet the forecasted ramp in LEAP engine shop visits, including five-year commitments of more than $1 billion USD by GE Aerospace and more than €1 billion EUR by Safran Aircraft Engines. Open Fan advances toward flight test demonstration CFM International announced today ahead of Farnborough International Airshow new design and test milestones reached for the RISE program, a suite of technologies in development for next-generation aircraft propulsion. July 17, 2026 GE Aerospace to Spotlight Future of Flight at Farnborough International Airshow 2026 GE Aerospace will showcase its commitment to building a more durable and efficient future of flight at the 2026 Farnborough International Airshow, highlighting next-generation technologies and breakthrough capabilities across commercial and defense aviation. GE Aerospace and UK Export Finance Launch New Financing Solution for Regional UK Shop Visits GE Aerospace and UK Export Finance (UKEF) today announced a first-of-its-kind framework for shop visit financing for airline customers leveraging GE Aerospace’s Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) sites in Wales and Scotland. This new program will enable airlines to access financing for their engine maintenance spend, with UKEF supporting $1 billion in financing over the next five years, supporting airlines with quicker decision making and greater predictability.

title: La Asociación. Entre el arte y el deporte de alto rendimiento
summary: Science Gallery Monterrey presenta La Asociación, un proyecto de Jaime Ruiz Martínez que explora la práctica artística desde los modelos [...]Leer más... from La Asociación. Entre el arte y el deporte de alto rendimiento
body_text: Science Gallery Monterrey presenta La Asociación, un proyecto de Jaime Ruiz Martínez que explora la práctica artística desde los modelos del deporte de alto rendimiento. Comisionada por la Colección FEMSA, La Asociación reúne arte, deporte, ciencia y tecnología, para explorar la competencia, la colaboración y las formas alternativas de aprendizaje, a través de una exposición, un proyecto de investigación y un laboratorio participativo. El proyecto comisionado por la Colección FEMSA reúne arte, deporte, ciencia y tecnología, para explorar la competencia, la colaboración y la práctica artística, a través de una exposición, un proyecto de investigación y un laboratorio participativo. Monterrey, Nuevo León (9 de julio de 2026) — A partir del 9 de julio, Science Gallery Monterrey presenta La Asociación, un proyecto de Jaime Ruiz Martínez comisionado por la Colección FEMSA. Concebida como una exposición, un proyecto de investigación y un laboratorio participativo, la iniciativa explora las dinámicas de colaboración, competencia y aprendizaje que atraviesan la práctica artística. La Asociación explora la práctica artística desde los modelos del deporte de alto rendimiento. Como parte de una investigación sobre la colectividad, la competencia y las formas alternativas de aprendizaje, el artista mexicano conformó una Selección Nacional de Artes Visuales ficticia, para la que convocó a dieciocho artistas a participar en una concentración que incluyó pruebas psicológicas, neurológicas y físicas, con el propósito de integrar un equipo nombrado el «onceideal». La investigación se desarrolló en colaboración con especialistas en Medicina del Deporte del Tecnológico de Monterrey y el Behavioral Research Lab, a través de la Iniciativa de Artes de la Escuela de Arquitectura, Arte y Diseño (EAAD), situando el proyecto en la intersección entre arte, ciencia y tecnología. Su objetivo es explorar cómo las y los artistas experimentan el estrés, la competencia, la retroalimentación y el rendimiento. A partir de estas mediciones, la propuesta también busca reflexionar sobre la práctica artística entendida como una actividad de alto rendimiento y, a su vez, como un espacio para la construcción colectiva de conocimiento. “La Asociación es un esfuerzo colectivo por indagar en un grupo de artistas y sus potencias sociales” Jaime Ruiz Martínez. A través de videos, imágenes, diagramas e instalaciones interactivas, La Asociación convierte la producción artística en un experimento social vivo y propone una mirada a las dimensiones psicológicas y físicas del trabajo creativo. Como parte del proyecto se empleó un sistema de electroencefalografía (EEG) de 256 canales, una tecnología de investigación altamente especializada y poco común en México, que permitió registrar y analizar la actividad cerebral de las y los artistas durante distintas pruebas. La investigación revela la profunda interconexión entre el cuerpo y la mente, mostrando cómo los procesos cognitivos y emocionales se reflejan a través de respuestas físicas, como la actividad cerebral, el ritmo cardíaco, la sudoración o la dilatación de la pupila. Esta aproximación, señaló Beto Díaz Suárez, curador de Colección FEMSA, surge de una pregunta que atraviesa todo el proyecto: «¿Qué pasaría si lxs artistas fueran considerados atletas de alto rendimiento? La Asociación pone en diálogo el arte con el deporte, la ciencia y la tecnología, para explorar cómo la competencia, la colaboración y el rendimiento atraviesan la práctica artística. Ese cruce entre disciplinas refleja el interés de la Colección FEMSA por impulsar investigaciones que respondan a preguntas contemporáneas y generen nuevas formas de reflexión, experimentación y construcción de comunidad». Presentada en Science Gallery Monterrey, la exposición reúne instalaciones, videos, diagramas, registros documentales, fotografías y experiencias participativas que invitan al público a involucrarse activamente con la investigación. En este sentido, dialoga con la misión de este espacio de promover el intercambio entre arte, ciencia y tecnología, para abordar problemáticas contemporáneas desde perspectivas experimentales, convirtiendo el espacio expositivo en un lugar de investigación activa en el que la experiencia estética se encuentra con la producción de conocimiento. Ubicada en la Planta Baja del edificio EXPEDITION FEMSA, dentro del Distrito de Innovación Monterrey del Tecnológico de Monterrey, un espacio territorial donde convergen talento, conocimiento y creatividad para impulsar soluciones a retos relevantes desde la investigación, la innovación y el emprendimiento. Science Gallery Monterrey abrió sus puertas en noviembre de 2024 como la primera sede de la red internacional Science Gallery en América Latina. Impulsada por la EAAD, la galería reúne proyectos de arte y ciencia que invitan a públicos jóvenes a dialogar con ideas que cuestionan el presente y proyectan futuros posibles. Como extensión del proyecto, Galería Abierta distritotec presenta una serie de imágenes inspiradas en la ficción del «onceideal». Ubicada en el espacio público, la intervención acerca el universo visual de La Asociación a la comunidad universitaria y a las y los visitantes de distritotec, generando nuevas formas de encuentro con algunas de las preguntas que articulan la investigación desarrollada en Science Gallery Monterrey. Comenta al respecto Miguel González Virgen, director de Science Gallery Monterrey: “En el proyecto de Jaime Ruiz tenemos la confluencia de las dos formas de pensar y hacer que distinguen las actividades de Science Gallery: el pensamiento intuitivo del arte, y la investigación de las ciencias. La colaboración de Jaime con el Behavioral Research Lab nos ofrece una perspectiva a la vez artística y científica de cómo diferentes artistas experimentan el juego del arte. Con el apoyo del investigador Pedro Cortés, el artista pudo medir científicamente las actividad neuronal y fisiológica de 18 artistas que conformaron una especie de Selección Nacional en el gran campeonato del arte.” La Asociación forma parte de los proyectos impulsados por la Colección FEMSA para fomentar la producción de nuevas obras e investigaciones que respondan a los desafíos y preguntas del presente. A través de su programa de comisiones, la Colección promueve procesos de colaboración interdisciplinaria que amplían el alcance del arte mediante la reflexión, la experimentación y la construcción de comunidad. ### Sobre Colección FEMSA Desde 1977, la Colección FEMSA ha construido un acervo referente en México y América Latina. Hoy, rumbo a su 50 aniversario, reafirma su compromiso con generar espacios de encuentro entre personas, ideas y comunidades. A lo largo de cinco décadas, ha sido un agente clave en la profesionalización del campo artístico y en la colaboración con instituciones dentro y fuera del país. Su historia está vinculada a espacios pioneros como el Museo de Monterrey (1977-2000), donde comenzó a consolidarse públicamente y donde se formaron los primeros núcleos de su acervo. Tras la conclusión de su etapa de museo, la Colección asumió un carácter itinerante, ampliando su presencia a través de colaboraciones con museos y organizaciones de diversas regiones. Este recorrido sentó las bases de apertura, colaboración y movilidad, que aún siguen definiendo a la institución. La Colección FEMSA tiene como propósito generar espacios de conexión, reflexión y diálogo a través del arte. Su acervo constituye el punto de partida para el desarrollo de propuestas y contenidos enfocados en la divulgación y la investigación de diversas manifestaciones artísticas, que permitan aproximaciones significativas al arte moderno y contemporáneo latinoamericano, así como fomentar el pensamiento crítico, la creatividad y la participación ciudadana. De cara al futuro, apuesta por incorporar miradas históricamente relegadas, fortalecer el diálogo con diversas audiencias, y desarrollar proyectos que respondan a los retos culturales, sociales y ambientales de nuestro tiempo. Acerca de FEMSA FEMSA es una empresa que genera valor económico y social por medio de empresas e instituciones, al tiempo que busca ser el mejor empleador y vecino de las comunidades en donde tiene presencia. Participa en la industria del comercio al detalle a través de la División Proximidad Américas, de la que forma parte OXXO, una cadena de tiendas de formato pequeño, y otros formatos minoristas relacionados; y Proximidad Europa, que incluye a Valora, nuestra unidad de retail europea que opera tiendas de conveniencia y foodvenience. En el comercio al detalle, FEMSA también participa a través de la División Salud que incluye farmacias y actividades relacionadas, y en Spin, que incluye Spin by OXXO y Spin Premia, entre otras iniciativas de servicios financieros digitales. Por otro lado, en la industria de bebidas participa operando Coca-Cola FEMSA, el embotellador de productos Coca-Cola más grande del mundo por volumen de ventas. A través de sus Unidades de Negocio, emplea a más de 392 mil colaboradores en 18 países. FEMSA es miembro del Índice Dow Jones Best-in-Class World Index y del Dow Jones Best-in-Class MILA Pacific Alliance Index, ambos de S&P Global; Índice FTSE4Good Emerging, Índice MSCI EM Latin America ESG Leaders, S&P/BMV Total México ESG, entre otros índices. Sobre Artes EAAD Su objetivo es estimular el desarrollo de los estudiantes del Tec de Monterrey mediante proyectos y estrategias artísticas contemporáneas vinculadas con la ciencia y la tecnología, fortaleciendo una cultura de bienestar integral, diversidad e inclusión en la comunidad Tec por medio de diversos proyectos trabajados desde la intervención de sitio, la instalación y el arte-objeto. Se distingue por vincular artistas con trayectoria y establecer alianzas con diversas instancias del Tecnológico de Monterrey, así como con actores gubernamentales, agentes de cooperación internacional, centros de pensamiento, fundaciones, organizaciones de la sociedad civil y empresas. Se articula como una red de nodos regionales en Monterrey, Ciudad de México, Guadalajara, Querétaro y Puebla, que desarrolla líneas curatoriales y programas situados en torno a cuatro ejes estratégicos: crear, por medio de laboratorios de experimentación artística transdisciplinar; educar, mediante una plataforma de formación continua; exponer, a través de espacios diversos, y promover, mediante la gestión de proyectos artísticos con impacto comunitario e institucional. Acerca de Science Gallery Monterrey Science Gallery Monterrey es un lugar donde el arte y la ciencia se cruzan para descubrir nuevas maneras de preguntar, comprender e imaginar el mundo que habitamos. Ubicada en el edificio Expedition FEMSA, dentro del Distrito de Innovación Monterrey del Tecnológico de Monterrey, la galería abrió sus puertas en noviembre de 2024 como la primera sede de la red Science Gallery en América Latina. Forma parte de la red internacional Science Gallery —con espacios en Londres (Reino Unido), Melbourne (Australia) y Bengaluru (India)— que reúne a artistas, científicos e investigadores en torno a una plataforma global donde convergen investigación, experimentación y participación pública. Impulsada por la EAAD, la galería presenta exposiciones, programas de aprendizaje y convocatorias abiertas que invitan a públicos jóvenes y diversos a dialogar con ideas que cuestionan el presente y proyectan futuros posibles. Sus exposiciones reúnen proyectos locales, nacionales e internacionales de arte y ciencia que generan conversaciones en torno a temas como los futuros, la tecnología, el cuerpo y la mente, el medio ambiente y las relaciones entre conocimiento, pensamiento y sociedad.

title: AI Interviewer for Technical Screening: A Practical Guide for Engineering Teams
summary: For engineering leaders, the cost of technical screening isn’t just recruiter time. It’s senior engineer...
body_text: Hiring Best Practices AI Interviewer for Technical Screening: A Practical Guide for Engineering Teams Written By Danielle Bechtel | July 17, 2026 For engineering leaders, the cost of technical screening isn’t just recruiter time. It’s senior engineer time. Every hour a staff engineer spends on a first-round phone screen is an hour not spent shipping. An AI interviewer built for technical screening can absorb a meaningful chunk of that early-stage load, but only if it’s configured to evaluate the things that actually predict engineering performance, not just whether code compiles. This guide is written for engineering managers and technical hiring leads deciding whether, and how, to bring AI-led screening into their pipeline. What “Technical Screening” Actually Needs to Measure A good technical screen isn’t just “can this person write correct code.” It’s evaluating several distinct signals at once: Problem decomposition: can the candidate break an ambiguous problem into a solvable structure? Correctness: does the solution actually work, including edge cases? Communication: can the candidate explain their reasoning as they work, not just present a finished answer? Adaptability: how does the candidate respond to a hint, a constraint change, or a follow-up question that pushes on their initial approach? An AI interviewer for technical roles needs to be evaluated against all four, not just correctness. A system that only checks whether output matches expected results is closer to an automated test grader than a true interviewer , and will miss a lot of what makes someone a strong engineering hire. Where AI Interviewers Fit in a Technical Hiring Funnel For most engineering orgs, the highest-leverage place for an AI interviewer is the first substantive technical touchpoint — after resume screening, before a live engineer-led round: Application → Resume/ATS screen → AI interviewer (technical screening round) → Live technical interview with engineer → System design / team-fit round → Offer This placement captures the biggest efficiency win — removing repetitive first-round screens from engineers’ calendars — while preserving live, human-led rounds for deeper technical evaluation and team fit, where nuance matters most. What Good Looks Like: Question Design for Technical AI Interviews Favor problems with multiple valid approaches. Questions with a single “correct” path are easy to grade automatically but produce weak signal. They don’t reveal how a candidate thinks. Look for problems that allow for a brute-force approach and a more optimized one, so the AI interviewer can evaluate reasoning quality, not just final output. Include follow-up and probing questions. A strong technical AI interviewer doesn’t just ask a question and grade the answer. It asks a natural follow-up (“what’s the time complexity here?” or “how would this change if the input were much larger?”) the way a human interviewer would, to test depth rather than memorized solutions. Calibrate difficulty to the actual role level. A question bank built for junior engineers won’t produce useful signal for senior candidates, and vice versa. Role-specific calibration matters more for technical screening than for most other interview types. Avoid trick questions and obscure trivia. Questions that test whether a candidate has memorized a specific language quirk rather than genuine problem-solving ability produce noisy signal and a poor candidate experience. Evaluating Whether an AI Interviewer Is Working for Technical Roles Once live, a few metrics indicate whether a technical AI interviewer is producing real signal: Correlation with downstream interview performance. Do candidates who score well in the AI interview also perform well in the live technical round? Low correlation suggests the rubric needs recalibration. False negative rate. Are strong candidates, as judged by later human rounds, getting screened out by the AI interviewer at a higher rate than expected? This is a critical thing to monitor, since a false negative here means losing a good candidate before a human ever sees them. Engineer time saved. Track hours of senior engineer time no longer spent on first-round screens, and reinvest that time in later-stage interviews where it adds more value. Candidate experience for technical candidates specifically. Engineers tend to be a discerning audience about tooling, a clunky AI interview experience can hurt employer brand with exactly the audience you’re trying to hire. Common Concerns from Engineering Teams “Will it miss strong candidates with unconventional backgrounds?” This is a legitimate risk if the rubric is calibrated too narrowly around a “typical” candidate profile. Mitigate it by validating the rubric against a diverse set of past hires, including successful engineers who didn’t follow a conventional path into the role. “Will candidates game it?” Any structured assessment can be prepared for, human-led or AI-led. The mitigation is the same either way: favor problems that test reasoning and adaptability over memorized patterns, and use follow-up questions that are harder to prepare for than the initial prompt. “Does this replace our take-home or live coding round?” In most mature setups, no. The AI interviewer typically replaces or supplements an early conversational screen, while a live coding or system design round with an engineer remains part of the process for candidates who advance. A Realistic Expectation An AI interviewer for technical screening works best as a well-calibrated first filter, not a final word. Used this way, it removes a genuine bottleneck — engineer time spent on repetitive early screens — while keeping the highest-stakes technical judgment calls in human hands, later in the process where more context is available. Getting Started If your engineering org is considering this, the highest-leverage first step is usually auditing your current first-round technical screen: how much senior engineer time it consumes, how consistent it is across interviewers, and where good candidates currently drop out due to scheduling friction. That audit will tell you whether an AI interviewer is solving a real bottleneck for your team or just adding a new step to an already-working process.
